note: The world critic under a historical name; audits against the bullets under ## Rules and nothing else.
orchestrator_note: The hardest audit of the run, and the only chapter whose central CLAIM is a rule claim: that nothing was forged and no rule was broken, and that the estate's line is now the law of the parish precisely because every procedure was obeyed. The critic was told that if any clause was in fact broken the chapter's claim was false and that was a high-severity finding, and was pointed at the load-bearing test by name - R5's signing clause, which requires that the entry be taken AFTER the light has come onto Raven Hause, because Dent and Fowler are dale-born and both sign. It traced the sequence both times and found the chapter lawful: Brock arrives in the dark, the light comes onto the fell, they cross, the entry is taken and signed in the light. Also confirmed: the theodolite stands where it was put and is found turned to the tower with the grass read for marks and none found; two witnesses at the station signing before the surveyor leaves it; the oak-to-tower angle governed by R2 rather than R1, and TRUE - a correct measurement put in the wrong place in an argument, which is the whole horror; and Hale's decision to leave the instrument out read as breaking a custom, which R5 says is what it is, rather than a law the dale enforces.
